text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Monday.

- 'Croatia expects investment from Kuwait', Croatian Prime Minister Zlatko Matesa said following an official visit to Kuwait last week. He said some concrete projects were agreed, in areas like infrastructure, tourism and construction.

- Jacques Klein, the American diplomat who runs the United Nations administration of Eastern Slavonia, the last Serb enclave in Croatia, said he would announce the local elections on Tuesday. Croatian government set the poll for April 13.

- Croatian cities are growing faster than the state wants them to, says the head of the Urban Planning Office, Matija Salaj. He goes on to say that many cities have become overpopulated and unfit for demographic development and organization of life. Zagreb has grown by 170,000 people over the past three years.
- Commentary: Foreign scholarships could lead to a brain drain after which Croatia might have to import experts.
- International travel fair in Berlin: German tourists expected to return en masse to the Adriatic. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
